sections.html:
Gillette is the county seat of Campbell County in northeastern Wyoming, with a 2020 census population of 33,403. The city grew outward in stages, and on January 1, 2018 it annexed the Antelope Valley-Crestview area, which pulled a large residential district inside city limits. Westover, Foothills and the Westover Road corridor are part of the built-up area.

The boundary decides which rulebook your house lives under. A home inside the city follows city zoning, city permits and city water and sewer rules. A home just outside falls under Campbell County instead. City planning staff say owners can petition to annex land that touches city limits, and extending services is generally at the owner's expense.

Gillette is a young city with few very old houses, since most of its growth came with energy development. If your home dates from a growth decade, look at the age of the roof, furnace and water heater before you list, because buyers will ask.

Coal, oil and coalbed methane have driven the local economy for decades, and much of the coal Wyoming ships comes out of the Powder River Basin around Gillette. When mine employment or coal prices shift, demand for houses can shift with it. A seller who has to move on a short clock may find fewer buyers in a slow stretch, which is one reason some owners prefer a cash sale with a known closing date.

Gillette has cold winters, hot dry summers and enough hail to matter. On May 26, 2010, a hail storm hit the Westover and Foothills subdivisions hardest, and the Gillette News-Record estimated the damage could top $46 million, including $28 million for roofs and gutters. Buyers here look closely at roof age and gutters.

Freeze and thaw cycles are hard on old windows, thin attic insulation and poor grading. Fixing or at least documenting those items before a buyer's inspector finds them keeps negotiations calmer.

Most structural work in Gillette needs both a building permit and a zoning permit, and unpermitted work can complicate a sale. A garage or addition needs both after review by Building Inspection and Planning. Decks, sheds and retaining walls usually need both too. A shed under 200 square feet or a retaining wall under 4 feet tall needs only the zoning permit.

Other city rules that come up in sales:

  • Fences need a free zoning permit. Front-yard fences are limited to 4 feet and side and rear fences to 6 feet.
  • Single-family zones allow one residence per lot, so a second dwelling on the property is not permitted.
  • Homes need at least two paved off-street parking spaces.
  • Home businesses in residential zones need a Home Occupation Permit from Code Compliance.

Call the Planning Division at (307) 686-5281 to check zoning. The Building Division is at (307) 686-5200 or gillette@gillettewy.gov, and permits and inspections go through the city's online portal. If the house has a converted garage, an unpermitted deck or a basement rental unit, ask early whether the work can be legalized or whether a buyer will discount for it.

sections.h2: Property tax due dates and exemptions
sections.html:
Campbell County follows the state calendar. The county treasurer mails tax bills on or before October 10. Paying everything by December 31 avoids delinquency on the first half.

InstallmentDue dateDelinquent after
First halfSeptember 1November 10
Second halfMarch 1May 10

Unpaid balances accrue 18 percent annual interest, so ask the Treasurer for the current terms before you close.

Homeowners, seniors and veterans can apply for 2027 exemptions from October 1, 2026 through March 1, 2027. The state Homeowner's Exemption removes 25 percent of taxable value on the first $1 million of fair market value for an owner-occupied primary residence. The Long-term Homeowner's Exemption removes 50 percent on the first $3 million for owners 65 or older who have paid Wyoming residential property tax for at least 25 years. The veteran's exemption is a $6,000 reduction in assessed value, with a filing deadline of the fourth Monday in May.

Call the Treasurer at (307) 682-7268 or the Assessor at (307) 682-7266. If you sell during the year, ask your title company how current-year tax will be handled at closing.

The Campbell County Clerk records deeds and keeps the grantor and grantee indexes. Under Wyoming Statute 18-3-402, the clerk stamps each instrument with the day, hour and minute it arrives, and the date of record is the filing date. The clerk will not record a document until the fee is paid. The Clerk's office phone is (307) 682-7285.

The city planning FAQ advises buyers to read the title report for easements, pre-annexation agreements and deed restrictions. You can save time by pulling the plat and any recorded agreements before listing.

If the house came through an estate, the paperwork that gives someone authority to sign the deed has to be in order before closing, so start that early.

sections.h2: Selling when taxes or liens are owed
sections.html:
Back taxes, a lien or a mortgage that is behind do not stop a sale, but they change the closing steps. The balance is paid from the proceeds at the title company, so you need a payoff figure first. Start with the Treasurer for the tax amount, and gather the mortgage statement and any lien paperwork.

Tell whoever you are selling to about these items at the start. A surprise at the title stage is what slows most closings down.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale compare with listing?
sections.html:
Gillette sellers commonly face aging roofs, deferred repairs, estate transfers and job moves. A cash sale works well when the owner wants to skip showings, repairs and a long financing contingency.

A cash offer from a company like ours is based on the house as it stands. We look at condition, location and the work a buyer would take on, and then we make an offer for you to accept or decline. There is no obligation, and we do not promise a specific price before we see the property.

  • Open-market listing: more exposure and often a higher price, with agent commission, repairs, showings and a financing timeline.
  • Cash sale: faster and simpler, usually at a lower price than a fully prepared listing.

Whichever route you choose, compare the numbers side by side before you sign.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Gillette house if it needs a new roof?
faqs.a: Yes. Hail has damaged many Gillette roofs, including the May 26, 2010 storm that hit Westover and Foothills. A cash buyer prices the roof into the offer, so you do not have to replace it before selling.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Campbell County?
faqs.a: The first half is due September 1 and the second half March 1. Taxes become delinquent after November 10 and May 10, and paying everything by December 31 avoids delinquency on the first half. Call the Treasurer at (307) 682-7268 to confirm your balance.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to sell a house with an unpermitted deck or garage in Gillette?
faqs.a: A permit is not required to sell, but unpermitted work can slow a sale or lower offers. Decks, additions and garages usually need building and zoning permits. Call the Building Division at (307) 686-5200 to ask whether work can be permitted after the fact.

faqs.q: Where are deeds recorded for a Gillette home?
faqs.a: Deeds are recorded with the Campbell County Clerk. The clerk stamps the date and time each instrument arrives and requires the fee in advance. The Clerk's office number is (307) 682-7285.

faqs.q: Does the Wyoming homeowner exemption affect my sale?
faqs.a: It lowers the taxable value while you live in the house as your primary residence, but it does not stop the sale. Ask your title company how tax is handled at closing.
